prompt.context: The client is a Canadian bank with 1000 branches. It is one of 6 large area banks. It recently decided to install ATMs in all of its branches. The research concerning the cost and vendors of choice has all been done.
prompt.question: How would you analyze the benefits from the ATMs, and what data would you need? Concentrate on the main issues.

clarifying_info.q: Are there cost savings associated with the use of ATMs? Could tellers be replaced or branches consolidated?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — 30% of tellers were redundant, and there is room for substantial savings by laying them off (salaries and benefits).

clarifying_info.q: Are competitors doing the same thing?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. Three of the client's largest competitors have installed ATMs in the last 2 days.

clarifying_info.q: Do customers want the service? How do they value it? Is this about acquiring new customers or retaining existing ones?
clarifying_info.a: In a recent survey: 20% of current customers would never use an ATM, 50% might use them, and the remaining 30% are so fed up that the bank does not have ATMs that they are about to leave the bank as customers.

clarifying_info.q: Could ATM-related data be used to offer new products (e.g., database creation, market segmentation)?
clarifying_info.a: This is something the client would need to look into.

framework: Company / Cost: Identify cost savings — teller headcount reduction (30% redundant), salary and benefits savings, potential branch consolidation, and more efficient transaction processing
Competitors: Assess competitive urgency — three of six major competitors have already installed ATMs in the last 2 days, creating a first-mover disadvantage risk
Customers: Segment customer response — 20% will never use ATMs, 50% are potential users, 30% are at immediate churn risk due to absence of ATMs
Technology: Evaluate longer-term upside — ATM data could enable customer databases, market segmentation, and new product development

questions.prompt: What are the cost savings from installing ATMs?
questions.guidance: With 30% of tellers redundant across 1000 branches, the savings are primarily in salaries and benefits. Candidate should quantify by estimating tellers per branch and average compensation, then multiply by 0.30. Should also note one-time severance costs offset against ongoing savings.

math.setup: Estimate tellers per branch × 1000 branches × 30% redundancy × average annual compensation per teller
steps: Assume ~5 tellers per branch × 1000 branches = 5,000 tellers total
Assume average fully-loaded cost (salary + benefits) ~$40,000/year per teller
math.answer: ~$60M/year in annual labor savings (illustrative; actual figures depend on Canadian bank labor costs provided)

questions.prompt: How urgent is the competitive response, and what is the customer retention risk?
questions.guidance: Three of six large competitors installed ATMs within 2 days — this signals rapid industry adoption. 30% of customers are at immediate churn risk. Candidate should flag that if those 30% skew toward high-net-worth or long-standing customers, the financial impact is disproportionately severe. Speed of action is critical.

questions.prompt: What should be done with branch space freed up by teller reduction?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will identify revenue-generating uses for vacated teller space: cross-selling new financial products (credit cards, investment services), or non-traditional offerings such as in-branch café or refreshment services. This demonstrates creative, out-of-the-box thinking.

brainstorming.prompt: What new products or services could the bank offer using the freed-up branch space and ATM customer data?

categories.name: Financial products
ideas: Credit card sign-ups at in-branch kiosks

categories.name: Non-traditional in-branch services
ideas: Café or refreshment stand (already being done by California banks)

categories.name: Data-driven opportunities
ideas: Customer segmentation database from ATM usage patterns
Targeted marketing campaigns for the 50% 'potential users'
Personalized product offers based on transaction history
Loyalty programs tied to ATM usage frequency

recommendation: The bank must act immediately given that 3 of 6 competitors have already installed ATMs and 30% of its customers are on the verge of leaving

Install ATMs as planned and launch a customer adoption campaign (advertising, promotions) to convert the 50% who might use them, since early data suggests technology-averse customers will need active encouragement
Capture the 30% cost savings from redundant tellers (~$60M/year illustratively), reallocating branch space to revenue-generating uses such as new financial products or in-branch amenities
risks: Technology aversion: customers who said they 'might' use ATMs may not actually adopt them, requiring ongoing promotional spend
Severance and transition costs offset short-term savings from teller reductions
If high-value customers are among the 30% at churn risk, loss of those relationships could exceed the cost savings
next_steps: Segment the at-risk 30% by customer lifetime value to prioritize outreach
Design an ATM adoption incentive program targeting the 50% potential users
Model severance costs vs. NPV of labor savings to confirm net positive economics
Explore data infrastructure needed to leverage ATM transaction data for new product development
